label: Official exchange rate
unit: bolivianos per U.S. dollar, period average
note: The BCB's official rate. Bolivia redenominated in 1987 (1 boliviano = 1,000,000 pesos bolivianos); the IMF series is in today's bolivianos throughout. Held at 6.86 to 6.96 from 2011 to early 2026, while a parallel market traded dollars at well above the official price from 2023; the official rate was moved to about 12 in mid-2026. No reliable monthly parallel-rate series is published (the IMF's crypto-based series for Bolivia tracks the official rate), so the book shows the official rate only.

label: Official exchange rate, end of period
note: The BCB's official rate at the end of each month.

label: Treasury bill yield
note: Yield on the BCB's open-market auctions of short-term government and BCB securities (Letras). Bolivia has no policy-rate target, and the auctions were rare from 2016 to 2025, so the book uses the interbank rate (money_market) as its policy-rate proxy.

note: Overnight interbank rate in bolivianos.

label: Real GDP, seasonally adjusted
source: INE Bolivia; seasonal adjustment by the book
note: INE's quarterly real GDP, seasonally adjusted by the book (robust STL decomposition of the log, period 4; adjusted = exp(log GDP - seasonal)).

label: Potential GDP (trend)
source: INE Bolivia; HP trend by the book
note: Hodrick-Prescott trend (lambda = 1600) of the log of seasonally adjusted real GDP. Bolivia publishes no potential GDP; HP trends are least reliable at the end of the sample.

label: Output gap
source: INE Bolivia; HP gap by the book
note: 100 x log(seasonally adjusted real GDP / HP trend), lambda = 1600, from INE's quarterly GDP.

label: Potential GDP (trend)
source: WDI + IMF WEO; HP trend by the book
note: Hodrick-Prescott trend (lambda = 100) of the log of real GDP, as for the output gap.

label: Output gap
source: WDI + IMF WEO; HP gap by the book
note: 100 x log(real GDP / HP trend), lambda = 100, on WDI real GDP 1960-2025 extended with the IMF WEO growth projections to 2031 (which softens the HP end-point problem). Bolivia publishes no output gap.

label: Structural budget balance
source: IMF WEO; adjusted for the cycle by the book
note: General government balance (IMF WEO) minus eps x output gap, with eps = revenue / GDP (revenue moves one for one with output, spending does not react). It ignores the swings of gas prices, which drive much of Bolivia's revenue.
